subject: Creating a Shiny Server package for Arch Linux

messages.subject: Creating a Shiny Server package for Arch Linux
parts:
Hello all,

I've started to put together a shiny-server-git package for Arch Linux to be submitted to the AUR:

    https://github.com/khughitt/pkgbuild/tree/master/shiny-server

I think I'm getting pretty close but have run into a couple issues trying to launch the server.

The first problem relates to the location of the node-posix package and is similar to that experienced by another user on the list:

$ shiny-server 

module.js:340
    throw err;
          ^
Error: Cannot find module '../../build/Release/posix'
    at Function.Module._resolveFilename (module.js:338:15)
    at Function.Module._load (module.js:280:25)
    at Module.require (module.js:364:17)
    at require (module.js:380:17)
    at Object.<anonymous> (/usr/local/shiny-server/lib/core/fsutil.js:16:13)
    at Module._compile (module.js:456:26)
    at Object.Module._extensions..js (module.js:474:10)
    at Module.load (module.js:356:32)
    at Function.Module._load (module.js:312:12)
    at Module.require (module.js:364:17)

The work-around suggested in the above-mentioned thread seems to resolve the issue:

git clone  https://github.com/melor/node-posix.git
npm build node-posix
sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/shiny-server/build/Release/
sudo mv node-posix /usr/local/shiny-server/build/Release/posix

However, now a different issue is now encountered when attempting to launch the server:

$ shiny-server                                                         
[2013-11-25 14:46:11.641] [INFO] shiny-server - Shiny Server v0.4.0.0 (Node.js v0.10.21)
[2013-11-25 14:46:11.643] [INFO] shiny-server - Using config file "/usr/local/shiny-server/config/default.config"
[2013-11-25 14:46:11.673] [ERROR] shiny-server - Error loading config: Object #<Object> has no method 'getpwuid'
[2013-11-25 14:46:11.674] [INFO] shiny-server - Shutting down worker processes

I don't have too much experience working with Node.js, so I'm a bit at a loss as to how to proceed from here.
 
Any suggestions?

Best,
Keith
